harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Deployed a 3-node RabbitMQ cluster (node1/node2/node3, AlmaLinux 9) with AMQP over TLS enforced by a cluster-dedicated CA. Server certs for each node (SAN=nodename+IP+localhost) and a client cert were issued from a self-created "RabbitMQ Cluster CA". rabbitmq.conf disables plaintext AMQP (listeners.tcp=none), serves AMQP only on 5671/TLS with ssl_options.verify=verify_peer and fail_if_no_peer_cert=true so only clients presenting a CA-issued cert can connect (verified: valid client cert accepted, no-cert and rogue self-signed cert both rejected with TLS alerts). The management UI (15672) is bound to each node's own cluster IP and firewalled via firewalld rich rules to the 10.100.48.0/24 cluster subnet only (confirmed reachable node-to-node, and inaccessible outside that scope by firewall policy). All three nodes are clustered (rabbitmqctl cluster_status shows all Running/Disc nodes) and an end-to-end mTLS AMQP publish/consume test succeeded on every node. Completed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol for all three nodes: captured pre-restart boot_id and healthy proof, issued a native `reboot` whose ack returned before disconnect, polled until each node was reachable again, confirmed boot_id changed, and verified rabbitmq-server became active with full 3/3 cluster quorum and working mTLS AMQP before moving to the next node.
actions_performed: Installed Erlang 26 and RabbitMQ 3.13.7 from official packagecloud repos on node1, node2, node3
Fixed /etc/hosts on all nodes using CLUSTER_HOSTS for name resolution
Wired inter-node SSH via CLUSTER_SSH_PUBKEY/PRIVKEY for cert/cookie distribution
Created a dedicated CA (RabbitMQ Cluster CA) and issued per-node server certs (SAN=name+IP+localhost) plus one client cert, all under /root/ca on node1
Distributed CA cert + per-node server cert/key to /etc/rabbitmq/tls on each node with rabbitmq:rabbitmq ownership and restrictive key permissions
Generated and distributed a shared Erlang cookie to all three nodes for clustering

Wrote rabbitmq.conf on each node: listeners.tcp=none, TLS-only AMQP on 5671 with verify_peer + fail_if_no_peer_cert=true, management.tcp.ip bound to the node's own cluster IP, classic_config peer discovery listing all three nodes
Enabled rabbitmq_management plugin and started rabbitmq-server on all nodes
Opened firewalld rich rules restricting 4369/25672/15672 to the 10.100.48.0/24 cluster subnet, and a plain port opening for 5671
Manually joined node2 and node3 to node1's cluster via rabbitmqctl join_cluster after automatic peer discovery initially failed due to firewall
Verified TLS/mTLS behavior with openssl s_client: valid client cert accepted, missing cert -> 'certificate required' alert, rogue self-signed cert -> 'Bad Certificate' alert
Created a RabbitMQ test user and ran an end-to-end AMQP-over-TLS publish/consume test with pika + client cert on all three nodes
Verified management API reachable from another cluster node (200 OK) confirming intra-cluster reachability

Executed the mandatory one-node-at-a-time restart protocol on node1, node2, node3: captured boot_id + health baseline, issued `reboot` via backgrounded ack, polled until reachable, confirmed changed boot_id, verified rabbitmq-server active and full 3/3 cluster quorum plus working mTLS AMQP after each restart

evidence.summary: node2 and node3 joined node1 via rabbitmqctl join_cluster; cluster_status shows all three as Disk Nodes and Running Nodes

evidence.requirement: AMQP served over TLS only, using a CA created for this cluster
evidence.summary: Created RabbitMQ Cluster CA, issued node certs, configured rabbitmq.conf with listeners.tcp=none and listeners.ssl.default=5671; ss/rabbitmqctl status shows only the TLS listener on 5671, no plaintext 5672

evidence.requirement: Only clients with a CA-issued certificate can connect
evidence.summary: TLS handshake without any client cert triggers 'certificate required' alert; a rogue self-signed cert triggers 'Bad Certificate' alert (confirmed in rabbitmq log); a CA-issued client cert completes handshake and a full AMQP publish/consume succeeds via pika+mTLS

evidence.requirement: Management interface reachable only from within the cluster
evidence.summary: Management bound to each node's own 10.100.48.x cluster IP (not 0.0.0.0); firewalld rich rule restricts port 15672 to the 10.100.48.0/24 cluster subnet; a cross-node request from node2 to node1:15672 succeeded (200 OK) proving intra-cluster reachability under that policy

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered cluster/services
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id f54d7366... and healthy mTLS AMQP baseline; issued reboot with early ack; connection reset confirmed disconnection; new boot_id d3a0b0e6... confirmed reboot; rabbitmq-server became active with full 3/3 running nodes and successful mTLS AMQP test

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered cluster/services
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id 717db5a2... and healthy baseline; issued reboot with early ack; disconnection observed; new boot_id 1560e3d1... confirmed reboot; rabbitmq-server active again with full 3/3 running nodes and successful mTLS AMQP test

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered cluster/services
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id 84419b90... and healthy baseline; issued reboot with early ack; disconnection observed; new boot_id 24282a0d... confirmed reboot; rabbitmq-server active again with full 3/3 running nodes and successful mTLS AMQP test

evidence.requirement: Final cluster-wide health and quorum after all restarts
evidence.summary: Post-restart-cycle check shows all three nodes (rabbit@node1, rabbit@node2, rabbit@node3) present in Running Nodes, TLS-only listener config intact, firewall rules intact
